query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Advanced CALPHAD modeling based on third-generation thermodynamic databases can efficiently predict melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase properties for high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Theoretical models of HEA compositions represented as homogeneous random solid solutions with expected configurational and vibrational contributions.
generation.intervention: Employ CALPHAD simulations that integrate updated thermodynamic parameters from both experimental fusion data and ab initio calculations, refining the Gibbs energy models to incorporate configurational and short-range order contributions.
generation.conditions: Simulations are performed over the full temperature range (from 0 K to above melting) for various HEA compositions, with iterative adjustment using validated experimental data from DSC and in situ measurements.
generation.structural_mediator: Calculated free energy versus temperature profiles that delineate the phase equilibrium between the solid and liquid states, capturing both enthalpic and entropic effects as well as volume-dependent terms.
generation.mechanism: Gibbs energy minimization, incorporating contributions from mixing enthalpy, thermal and configurational entropy, and volume changes, yields the melting point and latent heats through phase stability analysis.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fusion properties predicted with accuracy within ±5–10% compared to experimental measurements, enabling efficient and reliable screening of a wide HEA compositional space.
generation.baseline: Conventional CALPHAD assessments for binary and ternary systems using established third-generation databases (e.g., Ta-Cr and Ta-V) form the baseline.
generation.boundary: Accuracy is dependent on the quality and availability of thermodynamic input data; the approach may be less accurate for HEAs exhibiting complex short-range order or multiphase interactions not captured in current databases.
generation.uncertainty: Remaining uncertainties include potential oversimplifications of HEA interactions and limitations of the existing thermodynamic data, which may require additional experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Benchmark the CALPHAD-predicted fusion properties of several HEAs against comprehensive experimental data obtained from DSC and dilatometry across different crystal structures.
measurements: Volume change at melting from dilatometric data
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the CALPHAD predictions consistently deviate by more than 10% from experimental measurements, even after iterative refinement, the model approach must be considered invalid.

cited_evidence.text: Calphad [,,,] modeling was performed to compare with experimental results. Calphad-type thermodynamic database for rare earth sesquioxides was created by Zinkevich []. He critically reviewed all relevant experimental data available before 2006 and evaluated missing fusion enthalpies values based on measured enthalpy of fusion and volume change on melting for Y2O3. In a more recent evaluation by Zhang and Jung [] evaluation, missing data were estimated from liquidus in RE2O3-Al2O3 phase diagrams. However, new measurements for fusion enthalpies [] are in better agreement with Zinkevich’s assessment. Zhang and Jung’s evaluation varies largely with the values proposed by Konings et al. []. Zinkevich [] database for rare earth sesquioxides is openly available at the NIST website [] and was used in this work without any modifications. Thermo-Calc (Stockholm, Sweden) software was used for calculations.

We used an open-access database created by Zinkevich []. It is based on his 2007 assessments of thermodynamic properties of pure rare earth sesquioxides from room temperature to the melting point. This database is often used as a starting point for the creation of new thermodynamic assessments for systems with rare earth oxides [,]. Without any modifications, the database allows modeling of phase equilibria using the ideal solution model (which assumes zero enthalpies of mixing and the largest configurational entropy gains). A set of interaction parameters for the regular solution model (which accounts for mixing enthalpies) are included in the Zinkevich review [], but they are based on a limited number of selected binary systems, not included in the database [] and were not used in the present study. The phase fractions as a function of temperature from Calphad modeling are shown in Figure S14.

cited_evidence.text: The reliable thermodynamic properties of pure Cr and V are the essential inputs to establish their Gibbs energy expressions. Recently, the measured thermodynamic properties including heat capacity (Cp), heat content (HT–H298), enthalpy of fusion for pure Cr and V have been collected and reviewed by Obaied et al. [] and Arblaster [], respectively. The discrepancies of the measured data from different resources have been clearly clarified by them. Therefore, the reviewed thermodynamic properties are adopted in the present modeling. In addition, the thermal vacancy concentrations in pure Cr and V at their melting temperature were experimentally investigated by means of modulation and drop methods [,]. It is generally accepted that the effects of thermal vacancy on thermodynamic properties will become obvious with the temperature above 2/3Tm []. Thus, the expressions of defect-free Gibbs energy expressions (GiA2,df) in Equation (1) of pure Cr and V in their solid stable states (below Tm) were evaluated by fitting the experimental heat capacity from 0 K to 2/3Tm.
